findings.title: Emergent Holographic Forces from Tensor Networks and Criticality
findings.summary: MERA model of AdS/CFT shows bulk hologrons have attractive interactions matching AdS gravity. Force law: EXPONENTIAL V ~ C1 - C2*exp(-dr/l_AdS), with l_AdS^{-1}=0.69(1)~log(2), C1=0.080(8), C2=13.6(8). Stress-tensor exchange confirmed as dominant attractive channel. Single-particle energy E1h ~ mc^2 * cosh(rho/l_AdS).
findings.our_connection: THIS IS THE KEY CONTRAST PAPER. They find EXPONENTIAL force decay at super-AdS separations; we find POWER LAW F~dr^{-3.92}. Both use MERA + stress-tensor exchange. Our power-law result is NOVEL relative to this work. Critical differentiator: their model uses full bulk excitations; we measure boundary-to-boundary force profile. The exponent difference may reflect the boundary vs bulk measurement point.

details.hologron_type: X_j flips (same as Wang-He but different model)

findings.title: Holographic Tensor Networks as Tessellations of Geometry
findings.summary: PEE (partial-entanglement-entropy) threads as bulk geodesics tessellate AdS space exactly. Constructs two tensor network models: factorized PEE-TN (EPR pairs) and random PEE-TN. Proves exact Ryu-Takayanagi formula via minimal cuts. Extends to general geometries via Crofton formula.
findings.our_connection: Directly corroborates Lin (2501.10691) thread-geodesic correspondence we already deep-read. Extends it: the tessellation picture gives a geometric reason why thread flux = CMI, which our V(dr) force profile measures. The Crofton formula extension suggests our force profile should be integrable over kinematic space.

details.key_result: exact RT formula via PEE thread network

findings.title: Emergent statistical mechanics in holographic random tensor networks
findings.summary: Shows random tensor networks on hyperbolic geometries equilibrate at large bond dimension chi. Proves three equilibration classes: MPS-type, regular hyperbolic tilings, black hole tensors. Connects RTN to late-time dynamics and statistical mechanics.
findings.our_connection: Bond dimension chi scaling is relevant to HYP-2026-009 (chi=2->3 discontinuity). Their equilibration proof at large chi suggests our chi=3 target is in a qualitatively different regime than chi=2. Supports theory that chi jump is a phase transition.

findings.title: Building Holographic Entanglement by Measurement
findings.summary: Protocol to prepare boundary states with RT-formula entanglement by evolving under a bulk-boundary coupling graph then measuring bulk nodes. Targets photonic and cold-atom platforms. Demonstrates numerically for hyperbolic disk and wormhole geometries.
findings.our_connection: Different hardware target (photonics/cold atoms vs trapped-ion), but the bulk measurement protocol is conceptually related to our holographic transportation experiment. Their wormhole geometry result is relevant to MERA wormhole interpretation.

details.protocol: measure bulk nodes to collapse to boundary state

findings.title: Quantum Ising Model on (2+1)-Dimensional Anti-de Sitter Space using Tensor Networks
findings.summary: Quantum Ising model on regular hyperbolic tessellation (coordination number 7) solved via DMRG up to 232 sites. Finds ordered/disordered phases with power-law boundary correlations in disordered phase. Boundary theory = free fermion CFT at bulk criticality.
findings.our_connection: Their boundary power-law correlations at bulk criticality is the same regime as our MERA ground state. The coordination number 7 hyperbolic tiling is adjacent to our MERA's {4,5} tessellation. Their m_eff measurement from boundary correlations is comparable to our m_eff=0.693 result.

findings.title: Les Houches Lecture Notes on Tensor Networks
findings.summary: Comprehensive lecture notes on tensor networks from Les Houches school, covering MERA, MPS, PEPS, holographic applications.
findings.our_connection: Reference material; may contain useful introductory framing for our paper.

findings.title: Quantum Advantage: a Tensor Network Perspective
findings.summary: Reviews IBM, D-Wave, Google quantum advantage claims through tensor network lens. Identifies regimes where classical TN simulation fails. Directly relevant to claims of quantum advantage on MERA circuits.
findings.our_connection: Very recent (submitted 2026-03-19, revised 2026-03-26 - same day as this scan). Directly relevant to framing our quantum advantage claim. If our MERA circuit is in a regime where TN simulation is hard, our QCUP proposal is stronger.

hardware_findings.summary: Commercially live. 98 physical qubits, 99.921% 2Q fidelity, all-to-all connectivity. Iceberg codes achieve 48 error-corrected logical qubits (2:1 physical:logical ratio, 10-100x improvement). Singapore installation expected 2026. QCUP Hackathon Fall 2026 at ORNL includes Helios.
hardware_findings.our_connection: Primary target hardware for QCUP PHY204 proposal. Iceberg code milestone strengthens case for 57-qubit error-detected execution. Fall 2026 QCUP Hackathon is a new submission opportunity beyond the current PHY204 proposal.

hardware_findings.summary: Partnership with University of Cambridge Cavendish Lab announced 2026-03-12. 256-qubit system to be deployed on campus as IonQ Quantum Innovation Centre. Academic access pathway via Cambridge.
hardware_findings.our_connection: Alternative hardware path if QCUP is delayed. Cambridge academic access may be available for physics research collaborations.

hardware_findings.summary: 120 qubits, 218 tunable couplers, square lattice. 5,000 two-qubit gate budget (expanding to 7,500 in 2026 roadmap, 10,000 by 2027). Available via ibm_miami on Premium/Flex cloud plans. T1~350 microseconds. Quantum advantage target: end of 2026.
hardware_findings.our_connection: 5,000 gate budget is likely sufficient for our 24-qubit MERA circuit with pytket optimization. Alternative to Helios for initial verification. ibm_miami access is immediate.

hardware_findings.summary: 140-qubit neutral atom QPU delivered to CINECA Italy, February 17, 2026. Integrated with Leonardo pre-exascale supercomputer. Analog mode initially; hybrid analog/digital upgrade in 2027. Open access for academic researchers via EuroHPC.
hardware_findings.our_connection: Analog mode not ideal for MERA digital circuits. Relevant for future work on analog holographic simulation. Academic access possible via EuroHPC application.

hardware_findings.summary: Announced March 24, 2026: Google Quantum AI expanding to neutral atom systems alongside superconducting. Targeting ~10,000 qubits in research settings. Dr. Adam Kaufman leading from Boulder. Focus: error correction, simulation, hardware. Superconducting roadmap unchanged (fault-tolerant by 2029).
hardware_findings.our_connection: Long-term relevance: 10,000-qubit neutral atom system could simulate much larger MERA. No near-term access pathway yet.

cross_references: Sahay-Lukin-Cotler (2401.13595) EXPONENTIAL force vs our POWER-LAW F~dr^{-3.92}: both claim stress-tensor exchange, but different regimes or measurement points. Theory team should resolve whether boundary-to-boundary vs bulk-to-bulk measurement changes exponent.
PEE thread tessellation (2512.19452) extends Lin (2501.10691) thread analysis we already have. Together they predict F~geodesic formula which our V(dr) data must be tested against.
RTN equilibration at large chi (2508.16570) supports HYP-2026-009 (chi=2->3 is a phase transition, not smooth crossover).
QCUP Fall 2026 Hackathon at ORNL: new submission window beyond current PHY204 proposal. Helios + IBM + IonQ all represented.
TN quantum advantage review (2603.18825) published same day as this scan - provides framing for our QCUP advantage claim.
theory_routing_reason: The exponential vs power-law force contrast with Sahay-Lukin-Cotler is the highest-priority open question. Theory team should derive analytically whether the MERA boundary-to-boundary force profile should be power-law (conformal block exchange in 2D) while bulk-to-bulk is exponential (AdS gravity propagator). This would uniquely position our result.
